essence: A grey stone metropolis whose metal museum keeps a glass globe in every room, each holding a blue model of an ideal Fedora that someone once imagined and that became a toy before it could be built.
textDetails: Fedora is a metropolis of grey stone.
Its centre holds a metal palace, and every room of it contains a glass sphere (a crystal globe in Weaver).
Each globe contains a blue city: a model of a different Fedora.
They show forms the city could have had if circumstances had not made it what it is today.
Generation after generation, someone studied the Fedora of his day and devised a plan to make it ideal.
While he was still building his miniature, Fedora had already changed, and what had been a possible future was now just a toy in a glass sphere.
The palace of globes is now Fedora's museum; every inhabitant visits it and picks the city that matches his desires.
He imagines seeing himself reflected in the medusa (jellyfish) pond meant to collect the canal's water, had the canal not been drained.
Or riding high in a canopied seat along the avenue set aside for elephants, which have since been banished from the city.
Or sliding down the spiral of the snail-shell minaret, which never found a base to rise from.
Marco tells the Khan his map must find room for both the big stone Fedora and the little Fedoras in their globes.
The reason is not that they are equally real, but that every one of them is only a supposition.
The stone city embodies what people take as necessary before it actually is; the globes, what was conceived as possible and ceased to be so a minute later.
visualConcept: A dense, monochrome metropolis of grey stone (granite walls, slate roofs, damp flagstones, a tight old-town weave of streets) sits on a thick hewn-stone disc floating in an overcast void, and the only saturated colour anywhere is azure, coming from the centre. There stands the metal palace: an octagonal cast-iron building of three glazed storeys under an iron-and-glass dome, eight rooms to a floor, and in each of its 24 rooms a glass globe on a pedestal glowing blue, so the museum reads as a lantern of possible futures. Inside each globe is a tiny Fedora built in luminous azure, among them the three the text names: a city whose living canal fills a round pond of slowly pulsing jellyfish, a city with a broad avenue where elephants carrying high canopied seats process, and a city with a helical snail-shell minaret wound by a slide (it may hover a little above its blue roofs, baseless). The grey city carries the matching absences: a dry canal bed that runs in from the rim and stops dead at a plain paved square where the pond should be, a wide avenue lined with empty plinths and nothing walking on it, and a crowded block marked by a faint spiral inlay where the minaret's base was meant to be. The signature event makes the conceit literal: a full-scale azure projection of an ideal Fedora blooms over the stone, the stone city shifts beneath it until the plan no longer fits, and the projection shrinks and spirals into the museum to become one more globe. Entering a globe swaps the scales, so the blue toy becomes the world and the grey city becomes a distant memory.
layout: Base: hewn-stone disc of radius 23 and thickness 3.5 with an ashlar-coursed edge, floating. Centre: the museum (its form is interpretive; the text says only a metal building with a globe in every room), an octagon of circumradius 4.2, three storeys of 1.7 each and an iron-ribbed glass dome of radius 3.4, total height ~9.5; eight rooms per floor around a central atrium (24 rooms), each room's outer face glazed between riveted iron pilasters; one globe per room (diameter 0.55, glass with transmission, an inner azure miniature of ~40 instanced emissive boxes with edge lines), the three named globes enlarged to 0.8 on the ground floor facing the default camera. Plaza of grey flagstones from radius 4.2 to 7 with iron lamp posts glowing amber; a slow trickle of tiny visitors crosses it to the museum doors. Grey city from radius 7 to 22: ~1,100 instanced stone buildings, heights 1.2-5.5, mansard and gabled slate roofs, chimneys, irregular streets 0.4-0.8 wide, a few heavier civic blocks. Absences (interpretive): a dry canal bed 1.2 wide and 0.5 deep entering from the north-east rim and stopping at a plain paved square near (7, 0, -8); an elephant avenue 2.4 wide running straight from the south rim to the plaza between two rows of 10 empty plinths; a crowded block near (-11, 0, 3) with a faint spiral inlay in its paving. The rooms start with 20 lit globes and 4 empty pedestals that the cycle fills; then the oldest globe dims and empties so the loop continues. Hero globe contents: canal-and-pond city with ~30 pulsing jellyfish; avenue city with 6 elephants under canopied howdahs; minaret city with a helical tower wound by a slide and a tiny sliding figure.
signatureMotion: 1) From future to toy (every ~25 s): over some quarter of the grey city a full-scale azure projection grows, wireframe and translucent volumes of a new ideal plan rising above the roofs; as it settles, the stone city shifts beneath it (blocks rise or sink 0.5-2 units, a street kinks, scaffolding appears) until the plan no longer matches and its edges flicker; then it collapses, shrinking to a hundredth of its size as it spirals into the museum, and a new globe lights up in an empty room. 2) Life under glass: inside each globe something loops, jellyfish pulsing in the pond, elephants pacing their avenue, a tiny rider sliding down the minaret, while the stone city outside stays almost still. 3) Overcast breath: slow drifting fog, faint drizzle streaks, and the globes pulsing very softly, as if breathing.
interactionDescription: Flies the camera into the museum and through the glass of one of the three named globes (each toggle picks the next: pond, elephants, minaret). The grey city fades and the blue Fedora expands to fill the whole diorama, with the curved glass of the globe faintly visible overhead: you stand by the jellyfish pond fed by its living canal, watch elephants pass beneath canopied seats, or follow a rider down the spiral minaret. Toggling back shrinks the blue city into its sphere and returns the stone.
mood: Overcast late afternoon tipping toward dusk; flat, shadowless pewter light, a fine drizzle haze, stone slightly damp with a dull sheen; the museum glass glows azure from within and a few amber street lamps are newly lit around the plaza; quiet, contemplative, melancholy. Inside a globe: a clear, luminous blue dream, crisp and bright, like light seen through a glass marble.
caption: At the centre of grey Fedora stands a palace of metal, and in each of its rooms a glass globe holds a small blue Fedora that someone once drew as the ideal one. Each was a future until the stone city moved on before the model was finished. Citizens come to choose the one they would have loved: jellyfish in a pond fed by a canal now dry, elephants parading their avenue, a spiral minaret with nowhere to stand.
motto: The necessary is built in stone; the possible, kept under glass.
camera: Default: three-quarter view from the south-east, distance ~46, elevation ~32 degrees, target (0, 3, 0) so the glowing museum sits at the optical centre, with the dry canal leading in from the right and the empty elephant avenue running toward the lower left. Enter a Globe: a 4 s dolly to about 1.5 units from the chosen globe, a soft white-blue flare as the lens passes through the glass, then the blue city at full diorama scale in the same default framing, the globe's curved glass faintly visible as a reflection arc overhead.
